seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec titled 'Express uncertainty' describing when and how the assistant should express uncertainty or qualify answers

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_errors_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec titled 'Avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors' describing the assistant's duty to avoid mistakes that compromise accuracy or utility

expected_cross_links.name: express_uncertainty_section

expected_cross_links.name: avoid_errors_section

judgment_calls: Chose a 2-child split at L3040 rather than a 3-child split (e.g., at L3146) because the 'Highlight possible misalignments' section is a cohesive unit that should be read whole; a cut at L3146 would have split that section's examples from its principles.

The avoid_errors_section seed is established and used entirely within child 2; I carried it in seed_vocabulary because it appears in my span and my children need the name, but it does not cross a cut.
